subject: Agriculture
title: Sterile Insect Technique
description: A quick, practical guide to Sterile Insect Technique.

hook.text: What if you could wipe out a pest by flooding it with mates that can't reproduce? That's the sterile insect technique.

buildup.text: Males are sterilized with radiation, then released by the millions. Females mate with them and produce no offspring.

discovery.text: The US eradicated the screwworm fly from North America using this method in the 1960s—a historic triumph.

twist.text: SIT works best on islands or isolated areas. For widespread pests, the numbers needed are staggering.

climax.text: New genetic versions—using CRISPR gene drives—could make SIT far more powerful, and far more controversial.

punchline.text: Fight pests with pests. Turn reproduction into extinction.

quiz.question: How does the sterile insect technique control pests?
options: Releasing sterilized males that mate but produce no offspring

details.summary: The sterile insect technique (SIT) involves mass-rearing pest insects, sterilizing males with radiation, and releasing them to mate with wild females who then produce no offspring. This topic covers how SIT has eradicated screwworms and tsetse flies from entire regions.
details.whyItMatters: SIT is one of the most successful examples of pest eradication without chemicals. It eliminated the New World screwworm from North and Central America and is being deployed against fruit flies, mosquitoes, and other major pests.
takeaways: SIT releases sterilized male insects that mate with wild females, producing no offspring
It successfully eradicated the screwworm from North and Central America by the 1990s
Modern SIT programs target fruit flies, tsetse flies, and disease-carrying mosquitoes

faq.question: How does the sterile insect technique actually work?
faq.answer: Millions of male pest insects are mass-reared in factories, sterilized with controlled radiation doses that leave them healthy but infertile, then released into wild populations. Wild females that mate with sterile males produce no viable eggs, causing the population to crash over generations.

faq.question: What was the screwworm eradication program?
faq.answer: The New World screwworm laid eggs in livestock wounds, causing fatal infections. Starting in the 1950s, the U.S. released billions of sterile males over decades, pushing the pest southward through Mexico and Central America. By 1991, it was eradicated from the entire region.
